lede: From Vítkov to the Compacts. Stations with a source link lead into the texts; the others follow modern accounts and wait for their module.

stations.text: Žižka's men hold the hill above Prague against Sigismund's crusade; the crusade withdraws. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
The Taborites elect Nicholas of Pelhřimov their bishop, to give out the community's money according to each brother's need.
The Praguers defeat Sigismund's relief army below the royal fortress, which surrenders. 'I fear the peasants' flails,' a Moravian lord had warned the king.
Prague and Tábor storm Chomutov together; the men of the town are killed, and Taborite women burn the town's women in a vineyard hut.
Martin V sends Cardinal Branda to preach the crusade in Germany, with indulgences graded by who fights, who pays and who prays.
Žižka burns fifty Picards, men and women, at Klokoty near Tábor; they go to the fire laughing.
The estates of Bohemia and Moravia adopt the Four Articles, declare Sigismund unfit to rule and set up a regency of twenty. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Already blind in one eye, Žižka loses the other to an arrow at the siege of Rabí castle, and goes on commanding. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Surrounded at Kutná Hora, Žižka breaks out with his wagons and routs Sigismund's army at Německý Brod. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Žižka goes to eastern Bohemia and joins the Orebite brotherhood, which becomes his own. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
Žižka, some forty captains and lords and the councils of four towns issue their ordinance: orderly obedience, the booty shared, no person excepted.
Žižka defeats the army of Prague and its allied lords: Hussites against Hussites, fourteen hundred dead on both sides, by a royalist chronicler's count.
Žižka dies of illness near Přibyslav. His brotherhood calls itself the Orphans. (Modern accounts; module planned.)

The field armies destroy a Saxon and Meissen army before Ústí. In the same month the electors, meeting at Nuremberg, propose what is to be proclaimed in the crusading army: obedience, peace in the camp, no dice, no common women.
The third crusade, raised by the Frankfurt diet with its forty-eight articles of discipline, flees from Tachov before battle is joined. Prokop the Bald now leads the Taborite field army.
The imperial diet at Nuremberg orders its own war wagons: handguns, crossbows, flails, hooked pikes, and a chain to bind wagon to wagon.
The field armies raid Austria, Hungary, Silesia, Saxony and Franconia. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
The fifth crusade, with Cardinal Cesarini, breaks and flees at the sound of the approaching wagons. In a Latin song of the victory the cardinal advises the pope to grant three of the Four Articles.
A Hussite embassy with Prokop disputes the Four Articles before the Council of Basel. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
A Taborite foraging army is destroyed by the forces of the Upper Palatinate: a rare defeat in the field. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
The lords' league, Utraquist and Catholic, feigns flight; the field armies leave their wagons to pursue and are destroyed. Both Prokops fall. The foot had broken the ordinance's fifth article.
The Compacts of Basel are proclaimed; Sigismund is received as king of Bohemia. (Modern accounts; module planned.)
